title: The Old Man and the Sea
author: Ernest Hemingway

beats.event: Considered salao — 84 days without a fish
Manolin, forced onto a luckier boat, still tends his gear
Rows out early on the 85th day into the Gulf Stream
Catches an albacore, then hooks a huge marlin
Marlin too heavy to haul; it tows his skiff out to sea
First sight of the marlin — longer than his boat
Comes to love and respect his adversary
Third morning: the marlin begins to circle
Harpoons the marlin; lashes it alongside the boat
A mako shark tears a 40-pound bite from the marlin
Kills more sharks with a knife lashed to an oar
Sharks in a pack leave only bones behind
Reaches shore and staggers to his shack to sleep
Manolin weeps at the sight of him in the morning
A fisherman measures the skeleton at eighteen feet
